title: Patagonian Bay Scallops, Frozen, Wild Caught

content.title: About
content.content: Patagonian bay scallops are small marine bivalves that inhabit the cold southern ocean waters off the Patagonian coast. Wild‑caught and flash‑frozen shortly after harvest, they retain their natural flavor and nutritional profile. The scallops have a delicate, slightly sweet taste and a tender yet firm texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Patagonian bay scallops are smaller than the larger sea scallops and have a thinner shell.
Wild‑caught means the mollusks are harvested from their natural environment, not from aquaculture farms.
Freezing occurs within hours of capture, preserving most vitamins and minerals.
In Patagonia, scallops are traditionally hand‑collected using small boats and nets.
Scallops filter water, helping to improve water clarity in their ecosystem.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Scallops provide about 20 g of high‑quality protein per 100 g, making them an excellent protein source.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: They contain less than 1 g of fat per 100 g, most of which are beneficial polyunsaturated fatty acids.

items.title: Rich in vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is essential for nervous system health and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Mineral source
items.content: Scallops are a good source of zinc, iron, magnesium and selenium, supporting immunity and metabolism.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: They contain modest amounts of EPA and DHA, which benefit heart and brain health.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Possible toxin contamination
items.content: In rare cases, scallops can contain toxins if harvested from polluted waters; buy from reputable suppliers.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Scallops should be cooked thoroughly to eliminate bacteria and viruses.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Scallops can be quickly sautéed in butter, added to pasta, risotto or soups. They are also used in salads and as sushi fillings. Rinse under cold water before cooking; if frozen, thaw in the refrigerator.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen scallops at –18 °C or lower. Once thawed, use within 1–2 days and store in the refrigerator at 0–2 °C. Discard any scallops with off‑odors or discoloration.
